headline_en: How is the economy doing
summary_en: A question-and-answer explainer on Bangladesh's economy at the half-way point of fiscal year 2025-26, covering inflation, wages, GDP, credit, revenue, reserves, exports and imports. For migrants the usable part is the remittance and exchange-rate data: remittances topped USD 3 billion in December 2025, the first six months brought USD 16.26 billion (18% up), and the dollar is described as fairly stable at BDT 122.

facts.statement: Remittances sent by Bangladeshis abroad exceeded USD 3 billion in the month of December (2025), and inflows had been high for several months.
facts.source_in_article: Prothom Alo explainer citing Bangladesh Bank and other government sources

facts.statement: The record for remittances received in a single month was set in 'last March' (2025), when USD 329 crore (3.29 billion) came into Bangladesh, the highest for any single month so far.
facts.source_in_article: Prothom Alo explainer citing Bangladesh Bank and other government sources

facts.statement: In the first six months of fiscal year 2025-26 Bangladesh received USD 1,626 crore (16.26 billion) in remittances, 18 percent more than in the same period of the previous fiscal year.
facts.source_in_article: Prothom Alo explainer citing Bangladesh Bank and other government sources

facts.statement: The article says remittances have kept a positive trend since the fall of the Awami League government in August 2024.
The article says the dollar shortage in Bangladesh is almost gone and the dollar price has become roughly stable at BDT 122; the shortage had peaked during the Ukraine war.

Bangladesh's foreign exchange reserves stood at USD 31.18 billion at the end of December (2025), or USD 28.57 billion under the IMF's BPM method; remittance inflow and an improved current account are credited. Reserves had reached USD 48 billion in 2021 and had fallen to USD 26 billion when the Awami League government fell.
facts.source_in_article: Prothom Alo explainer citing Bangladesh Bank

facts.statement: Overall inflation in Bangladesh was 8.49 percent in December (2025), with food inflation 7.71 percent and non-food inflation 9.13 percent; rice inflation was 11.92 percent (12.26 percent in November); the national wage growth rate was 8.08 percent, below inflation.
Bangladesh's goods exports fell 14 percent in December (2025) to USD 397 crore from USD 462 crore a year earlier, the fifth straight monthly fall; imports that month were USD 5.80 billion.
facts.source_in_article: Prothom Alo explainer citing EPB and Bangladesh Bank

facts.statement: GDP growth in the first quarter of fiscal year 2025-26 was 4.5 percent, against 2.58 percent a year earlier; the article says weak private credit (6.58 percent growth in November) is shrinking private-sector job opportunities at home.
facts.source_in_article: BBS and Bangladesh Bank, via Prothom Alo explainer

key_quote_bn: চলতি অর্থবছরের প্রথম ছয় মাসে দেশে এসেছে ১ হাজার ৬২৬ কোটি ডলারের প্রবাসী আয়, যা আগের অর্থবছরের একই সময়ের তুলনায় ১৮ শতাংশ বেশি।

headline_en: Gunfight between two sides at a human traffickers' den, young woman killed
summary_en: On Friday 16 January 2026 an 18-year-old local woman was shot dead in Baharchhara, Teknaf, Cox's Bazar during a gunfight between armed men living in the hills and a human-trafficking gang. A local union member said the traffickers had gathered people in a hill hideout to send them to Malaysia by sea. Police said Baharchhara has become the main base of trafficking gangs; no one had been arrested.

facts.statement: Sumaiya Akter (18), daughter of Md. Siddique of Noakhaliya Para, Baharchhara union, Teknaf, Cox's Bazar, was shot dead at about 6:30 pm on Friday 16 January 2026 at the foot of the hill in Noakhaliya Para during a gunfight between armed men in the hills and members of a human-trafficking gang; she had two bullet wounds and was declared dead at Teknaf Upazila Health Complex.
facts.source_in_article: Cox's Bazar district police spokesperson Additional SP (DSB) Alok Biswas; emergency doctor Nowshad Alam

facts.statement: According to a Baharchhara union ward 9 member, trafficking gang members had gathered some people in a hideout in the hills of Baharchhara, Teknaf, to traffic them to Malaysia by sea; armed men living in the hills raided the hideout on hearing of it, which started the gunfight.
facts.source_in_article: Md. Ilias, member, ward 9, Baharchhara Union Parishad

facts.statement: Cox's Bazar police say the coastal Baharchhara area of Teknaf has turned into the main base of human-trafficking gangs.
facts.source_in_article: Additional SP (DSB) Alok Biswas, Cox's Bazar district police spokesperson

facts.statement: Police and other law-enforcement forces were running an operation in the Baharchhara hills to catch the armed men and the traffickers, but as of the evening of 16 January 2026 no one had been arrested; Teknaf Model Thana OC Md. Saiful Islam said legal action would be taken and the body was being sent to Cox's Bazar Sadar Hospital morgue for post-mortem.
facts.source_in_article: Additional SP Alok Biswas; OC Md. Saiful Islam, Teknaf Model Thana

key_quote_bn: সাগরপথে মালয়েশিয়া পাচারের জন্য মানব পাচারকারী চক্রের সদস্যরা কিছু লোকজনকে পাহাড়ের আস্তানায় জড়ো করে রাখেন।

headline_en: Lakhs of Bangladeshis 'will be harmed' by US visa suspension
summary_en: The United States has suspended immigrant visas for applicants from 75 countries including Bangladesh from 21 January 2026; tourist and other short-term visas are not covered. Three US immigration lawyers told Prothom Alo that lakhs of Bangladeshis with pending family-based petitions will be affected, while student, visit and business visas remain open and may be processed faster. The article gives figures on US visas and permanent residence granted to Bangladeshis and on remittances from the US.

facts.statement: The United States has suspended immigrant visas for applicants from 75 countries including Bangladesh, effective 21 January (2026); tourist or short-term visa holders are not covered by the restriction.
facts.source_in_article: Prothom Alo report; US State Department statement

facts.statement: The article explains that a US immigrant visa is one with which a person enters the US directly with a green card and becomes a permanent resident; it covers family-based green cards (spouse, parents, children, siblings) and employment-based permanent residence. Non-immigrant visas are for temporary stay and include student visas, visit visas and work visas.

Under the suspension, processing of pending petitions by naturalised Bangladeshi-Americans to bring parents, siblings, spouses or children to the US will stay suspended and family members cannot go for now. New family petitions can still be filed, but visas will not be issued for now; US citizens who newly marry cannot bring their spouse for now.
facts.source_in_article: US immigration lawyers interviewed by Prothom Alo

facts.statement: Immigration law expert Dilli Raj Bhatta says those affected include people whose cases have been pending for many years, those on the waiting list for immigrant visa review, and those whose interviews were already scheduled. He said there is no specific announcement on how long the policy will last and that lawsuits challenging it are expected.
facts.source_in_article: Dilli Raj Bhatta, Nepali-origin US citizen and immigration law expert

facts.statement: Lawyers say visas outside the immigrant category are not suspended: temporary, tourist and business visas are unaffected, so people who want to travel, study or go on business to the US can apply and will get a visa if eligible.
facts.source_in_article: US immigration lawyers interviewed by Prothom Alo

facts.statement: US immigration lawyer Raju Mahajan says that because immigrant visa processing is stopped, pressure on the embassy will fall and eligible applicants for other visas (travel, business, student) will get visas in less time than before; those who want to invest in the US can also apply as foreign investment is being encouraged.

Lawyer Moin Chowdhury called the suspension an inhumane decision: a wife married now cannot come, a child who passes age 21 will not be able to come, and a long suspension will create complicated problems.
facts.source_in_article: Moin Chowdhury, described as the first Bangladeshi-origin American lawyer licensed by the US Supreme Court

facts.statement: In US fiscal year 2023 about 59,254 US visas were issued to Bangladeshi nationals: 44,674 non-immigrant visas and 14,580 immigrant visas.
US Homeland Security statistics show Bangladeshis granted lawful permanent residence in the US: 14,890 in fiscal 2019, 9,010 in 2020, 6,180 in 2021, 10,140 in 2022 and 18,240 in 2023.
facts.source_in_article: US Office of Homeland Security statistics

facts.statement: Lawyers say some Bangladeshi families have petitions pending for 15 to 16 members, so by that reckoning several lakh people are waiting to immigrate to the US in stages.
facts.source_in_article: US immigration lawyers interviewed by Prothom Alo

facts.statement: Bangladesh received its highest-ever remittances 'last year': USD 3,282 crore (32.82 billion). The United States was the fourth-largest source, with 11 percent of remittances.

The US State Department said in a statement that immigrant visa processing for 75 countries would stay suspended while it reassesses its immigration processing so that no foreign national enters who may take public welfare funds and benefits; lawyers said the reason is that many who take citizenship draw government allowances instead of earning.
facts.source_in_article: US State Department statement; US immigration lawyers

key_quote_bn: অভিবাসী ভিসা স্থগিত হলেও এর বাইরে যেসব ভিসা আছে, তা স্থগিত হয়নি।

headline_en: May Bangladesh School Muscat meet Bangladeshis' expectations
summary_en: A reader's opinion piece by a Bangladeshi community figure in Oman about Bangladesh School Muscat after its governing-body election on 31 October 2025. It describes how the school was founded in 1996 with expatriates' donations collected through embassy services, how it is governed, its low fees, about 1,000 families using it, and complaints about falling standards, late audits and weak A-level teaching. It also notes a new, larger plot allotted for the school in Bowshar and the arrival of a new ambassador in February 2025.

facts.statement: Bangladesh School Muscat, a community school for children of Bangladeshis in Oman, was established on 3 September 1996 and formally inaugurated on 9 November 1996, with approval of Oman's Ministry of Education; it is run under Oman's policies for community schools.
facts.source_in_article: Writer Syed Mohammad Monjurul Islam, former joint secretary of Bangladesh Social Club

facts.statement: To build the school's new building, expatriate Bangladeshis in Oman gave donations to the Bangladesh embassy for 10 years: the writer says 5 rial was taken from each passport service, expatriates twice donated 10 rial, and the money was taken as a percentage from various embassy services over 10 years.

Bangladesh School Muscat is governed by five representatives directly elected by parents for two years plus three Bangladesh embassy representatives (one embassy representative and two highly educated Bangladeshi expatriates); the principal is ex officio member-secretary; the five elected members choose a chairman; the constitution requires a yearly audit.
The election of the governing body of Bangladesh School Muscat was held on 31 October (2025); five members won in the parents' vote.

The writer says Bangladesh School Muscat's tuition fees are much lower than other international schools in Muscat and about 1,000 families send their children there; teachers at the best schools are said to be paid three times what Bangladesh School pays.

Complaints listed about Bangladesh School Muscat: its standard has fallen (it once ranked number 4 in Oman, per the writer), there is a shortage of good A-level teachers and parents say A-level teaching is not up to standard, the 2023-24 audit was not done on time, there is waste and no proper accountability, the school ran for years without a principal, and its finances are fragile. Parents demand an audit of four years of alleged financial irregularities by a reputable firm.

Parents' wishes listed for the school include trained and better-paid teachers, a new building on a new site, a school bus, introduction of the English version of Bangladesh's national curriculum, and low-cost places for poor meritorious students; the writer says fees should be raised if needed. The article refers to O level and A level being taught there.

After a meeting at 11 am on 4 August 2024 between Bangladesh's ambassador to Oman Md. Nazmul Islam and Oman's Minister of Housing and Urban Planning Khalfan bin Said bin Mubarak Al-Shueili, the minister allotted a 9,079 square metre plot at Al Ansab in the Bowshar area for Bangladesh School Muscat's own building, larger than the plot allotted earlier.

Rear Admiral Khandaker Misbaul Azim became Bangladesh's new ambassador to Oman in February 2025; the writer says embassy service in Oman has visibly changed a great deal since his arrival, and that a retired Sri Lankan navy rear admiral (Pradeep Rathnayake) was appointed principal in August 2025. No Bangladeshi principal has been appointed since 2009.

key_quote_bn: মাসকাটের অন্য আন্তর্জাতিক স্কুলের টিউশন ফির তুলনায় বাংলাদেশ স্কুলের ফি অনেক কম।

headline_en: Immigration police stop 22 Bangladeshi workers at the airport
summary_en: On Saturday 1 November 2025 immigration police at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport stopped 22 of a group of 30 Bangladeshi workers travelling to Sri Lanka through China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation (CCECC) for an ADB-funded project. Police said their visas carried the words 'No work permit'; the company's recruitment representative said the group had BMET certificates and no-objection letters from both embassies and called it harassment, noting eight others left with the same documents.

facts.statement: At about 8 pm on Saturday 1 November 2025, immigration police at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, Dhaka, stopped 22 people who were leaving for Sri Lanka on worker visas; police said they were stopped because they had no permission to work.

The group of 30 Bangladeshi workers was going to Sri Lanka through China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation (CCECC) to work on a two-year project financed by the Asian Development Bank (ADB); they were to fly at 8:10 pm on an IndiGo flight via Chennai. Eight of the 30 departed; 22 were stopped.
The 22 workers stopped at Dhaka airport were told by the airport immigration authority, citing visa complications, to bring a clearance from the head office of the police Special Branch.

A Special Branch (immigration) police officer said the stopped workers' visas did not carry permission to work: the words 'No work permit' were written on the visas, and that was why they were stopped.
facts.source_in_article: An unnamed officer of police Special Branch (immigration)

facts.statement: CCECC's South Asian recruitment representative Mahbub Alam said the group had all valid papers, including BMET certificates and no-objection letters from the embassies of both countries, that the other eight went with the same documents, that it was plainly harassment, and that the workers suffered financial loss.
facts.source_in_article: Mahbub Alam, South Asian recruitment representative, CCECC

named_actors.name: China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation (CCECC)
named_actors.what_the_article_says: Was sending a group of 30 Bangladeshi workers to Sri Lanka for a two-year ADB-financed project; 22 were stopped at Dhaka airport on 1 November 2025.

named_actors.name: Mahbub Alam
named_actors.what_the_article_says: South Asian recruitment representative of CCECC; said the workers had BMET certificates and both embassies' no-objection letters and called the stop harassment.

key_quote_bn: তাঁদের ভিসায় লেখা ছিল ‘নো ওয়ার্ক পারমিট’। এ জন্য তাঁদের আটকে দেওয়া হয়েছে।

headline_en: Kuwait embassy's 'double holiday' policy makes expatriates' lives miserable
summary_en: A letter from a Bangladeshi social worker in Kuwait complains that the Bangladesh embassy in Kuwait closes on Kuwait's weekend, all Bangladeshi public holidays and all Kuwaiti public holidays, leaving few service days for more than three lakh workers. He says e-passport appointments are often unavailable online or come four to five months later, and proposes limited Friday service, more staff and restarting mobile consular camps.

facts.statement: The letter writer says more than three lakh (300,000) expatriate Bangladeshis are currently working in Kuwait.
facts.source_in_article: Md. Saiful Islam, social worker, Bangladeshi expatriate in Kuwait

facts.statement: Through the Bangladesh embassy in Kuwait, expatriates mainly get passport renewal (e-passport service), national identity card (NID), birth registration, visa attestation and out pass (travel permit), among other essential services.

Since e-passport service began at the Bangladesh embassy in Kuwait, expatriates face heavy crowds and wait for hours in long queues; an online appointment for an e-passport application is unavailable most of the time, and when one is obtained it is for four to five months later.

The Bangladesh embassy in Kuwait is closed on Kuwait's weekly holidays (every Friday and Saturday), on all Bangladeshi public holidays and on all Kuwaiti public holidays, which the writer says leaves very limited service days and makes it hard for workers who must take leave on a working day.
Mobile consular service or camps in different areas of Kuwait existed for some time earlier but, according to the letter writer, have been stopped for a long time.

The writer proposes that the embassy in Kuwait keep passport or selected urgent services open for limited hours on Fridays (with special allowance for staff), hire extra staff and digitise services, and hold frequent mobile consular camps in different areas of Kuwait.

key_quote_bn: অ্যাপয়েন্টমেন্ট পেলেও চার-পাঁচ মাস পরে পাওয়া যাচ্ছে।

headline_en: Professor Yunus to address the UN; reform and election may get emphasis
summary_en: A report on Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus's programme at the 80th UN General Assembly in New York, including his planned speech and a dinner on labour reform. The migration-relevant part: on Thursday 25 September 2025 Albania's President Bajram Begaj told Yunus that Albania wants to recruit skilled and unskilled Bangladeshi workers, is considering e-visas for Bangladeshis, and that its universities will welcome Bangladeshi students; Bangladeshis currently have to go to New Delhi for Albanian visas.

facts.statement: Albania expressed deep interest in recruiting skilled and unskilled workers from Bangladesh to meet its growing labour demand; President Bajram Begaj made the proposal in a meeting with Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus at UN Headquarters in New York on Thursday 25 September 2025, on the sidelines of the 80th UN General Assembly.
facts.source_in_article: Prothom Alo report of the meeting

facts.statement: Albanian President Bajram Begaj said: 'Our country needs labour. Several Albanian companies have already applied to recruit workers from Bangladesh.' He said cooperation could expand, especially in tourism.
Chief Adviser Yunus noted that Bangladeshi nationals currently have to travel as far as New Delhi for an Albanian visa, and asked the Albanian government to simplify the visa process.
President Begaj said Albania is considering introducing e-visas for Bangladeshis.

Asif Nazrul, the adviser in charge of the expatriates' welfare ministry, said Bangladesh can supply a varied workforce from doctors and nurses to factory and agriculture workers, and stressed signing a memorandum of understanding with Albania; the article does not report an MoU being signed.
President Begaj said Albania's universities are ready to welcome Bangladeshi students under the existing arrangement for admitting international students.

At a dinner hosted by Bangladesh's permanent mission at UN Headquarters on Thursday 25 September 2025, Yunus reaffirmed the interim government's commitment to implement key labour reforms in line with ILO conventions before the national election due in February; BNP, Jamaat-e-Islami and NCP leaders agreed labour-sector reform should continue.

key_quote_bn: বর্তমানে বাংলাদেশি নাগরিকদের ভিসার জন্য নয়াদিল্লি পর্যন্ত যেতে হয় বলেও উল্লেখ করেন।

headline_en: Why new chairman Arifur Rahman left Premier Bank and came back
summary_en: A profile of physician Arifur Rahman, appointed chairman of Premier Bank in August 2025 after Bangladesh Bank installed a new board. He recounts how, while working as a doctor in Saudi Arabia, he became involved in recruiting Bangladeshi workers for Saudi employers, was detained for about three months by Saudi police because that broke his iqama rules, and then ran a recruiting business under Saudi royal sponsors until 2010. The rest concerns the bank's bad loans and alleged embezzlement by former chairman H B M Iqbal.

facts.statement: Arifur Rahman, a Bangladeshi physician who worked at Saudi Arabia's National Guard Medical Services (clinic between Dammam and Al Khobar), says a wealthy contractor named Al Khodari, who had won the Saudi government contract to clean Dammam city, told him he needed 2,700 people from Bangladesh; Rahman later connected him with Riazul Islam from Dhaka, and Al Khodari divided the job of bringing the 2,700 workers among several people.
facts.source_in_article: Arifur Rahman, chairman of Premier Bank, speaking to Prothom Alo on 30 August 2025

facts.statement: After that became known, businessmen Ali Asgar Lobi, Nur Ali, H B M Iqbal, A H M Mustafa Kamal and M A H Selim, among others, came to Arifur Rahman one after another; a further job to take 4,000 people then came and was also shared among several of them.
facts.source_in_article: Prothom Alo report quoting Arifur Rahman

facts.statement: Some Pakistanis filed a complaint that Arifur Rahman, though a doctor, was involved in manpower export from Bangladesh to Saudi Arabia; the article says this was a breach of the rules of his iqama (Saudi residence permit), which he did not know.
facts.source_in_article: Prothom Alo report quoting Arifur Rahman

facts.statement: Following the complaint, Saudi police took Arifur Rahman away and interrogated him as a suspect; as the allegation was not proved he was released after about three months and rejoined his job.

Arifur Rahman says Saudi prince Mishari bin Saud bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, then head of the National Guard, asked him to run a business as recruiting manager for his elder brother Mishaal bin Saud bin Abdulaziz Al Saud; with Saudi policy support he obtained visas for Bangladesh, cutting into the shares of India, Pakistan and Thailand, and this continued until 2010.

Arifur Rahman claims that, combining cooperation with other recruiters of the time and his own work, about 17 lakh (1.7 million) Bangladeshis had got jobs in Saudi Arabia by then; he says a 2004 UNDP report described his contribution to sending 15 lakh people and the number later rose by two lakh.

Arifur Rahman bought a large share of Premier Bank with income from manpower export. Bangladesh Bank appointed a team led by him to the bank on 19 August 2025 and the new directors made him chairman on 21 August 2025; he says the bank's default loan rate is close to 23 percent and it could not pay a dividend this time.

headline_en: Malaysia may give Bangladeshi students the Graduate Plus visa
summary_en: On Wednesday 13 August 2025 Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus raised with Malaysia's Higher Education Minister Zambry Abdul Kadir the introduction of Malaysia's Graduate Plus visa for Bangladeshi students. Adviser Asif Nazrul said the minister agreed in principle, but formalities remain before it takes effect. About 10,000 Bangladeshi students study in Malaysia and, unlike students of other countries, cannot enter its labour market.

facts.statement: Malaysia's Higher Education Minister Zambry Abdul Kadir agreed in principle to give the Graduate Plus visa to Bangladeshi students studying in Malaysia, after Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus raised it at a meeting at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia, Kuala Lumpur, on Wednesday 13 August 2025; both sides must complete some formalities before the policy takes effect.
facts.source_in_article: Asif Nazrul, expatriates' welfare and overseas employment adviser

facts.statement: At present Bangladeshi students in Malaysia are denied the opportunity to enter Malaysia's labour market, whereas students of other countries get it; the Graduate Plus visa would let thousands of graduates take high-skilled employment there.
About 10,000 Bangladeshi students are currently studying at various universities in Malaysia.

Malaysia's Education Minister Fadhlina binti Sidek met Yunus at a Kuala Lumpur hotel on 13 August 2025; they discussed increasing scholarships for Bangladeshi students at Malaysian universities and colleges.

key_quote_bn: নীতিগতভাবে তিনি মালয়েশিয়ায় বাংলাদেশি শিক্ষার্থীদের জন্য গ্র্যাজুয়েট প্লাস ভিসা দেওয়ার বিষয়ে সম্মতি দিয়েছেন।

headline_en: UK introduces e-visa for foreign students
summary_en: The UK has replaced paper visa documents with e-visas for students: those who applied for a UK student visa from Bangladesh on or after 15 July 2025 no longer get a visa sticker (vignette) in the passport. Dependants of students still get vignette stickers. The article lists what students should do before flying, including creating a UKVI account linked to the travel passport.

facts.statement: From 15 July (2025), people who apply for a UK student visa from Bangladesh no longer receive a visa sticker (vignette) in the passport; the UK has introduced an e-visa system in place of paper documents.
facts.source_in_article: UK government, cited via Economic Times

facts.statement: The UK has already abolished the Biometric Residence Permit (BRP) and replaced it with the e-visa; the Biometric Residence Card (BRC) and passport stamps or sticker visas will all be replaced by e-visas in phases.
facts.source_in_article: UK government, cited via Economic Times

facts.statement: All the student's visa information is stored in a secure digital account, which can be checked or updated at any time; on entering the UK students need to carry only the passport and their e-visa account details.
facts.source_in_article: Prothom Alo report citing the UK government

facts.statement: Most applicants will receive an e-visa, but applicants who are dependants of students (husband/wife, children) will still receive a vignette sticker.

Before boarding, students going to the UK should: create a UKVI account and link the passport they will travel with; confirm the e-visa has been issued and is correctly linked to the account; carry a printed or digital copy of the e-visa approval letter to show at the airport or immigration; and update passport details in the UKVI profile if they have a new or changed passport.

The UK Home Office says the aim of the change is to make access easier and more secure and to advance digitisation; with an e-visa the visa can be verified or details updated at any time from anywhere.

key_quote_bn: যুক্তরাজ্যে প্রবেশের সময় শিক্ষার্থীদের কাছে কেবল পাসপোর্ট এবং ই-ভিসা অ্যাকাউন্টের তথ্য রাখতে হবে।

headline_en: Kushtia's Robijul, known for seven marriages, arrested in human trafficking case
summary_en: Police arrested Robijul Islam (40) of Kushtia on Sunday 20 July 2025; he faces at least six human trafficking cases. Police say he spent about twelve years in Libya, acted as the channel taking young men from Kushtia, Chuadanga, Jhenaidah and nearby districts to Libya, and that the ring filmed victims suffering in Libya and sent the videos to families to demand large sums.

facts.statement: Robijul Islam (40), of Patikabari village, Kushtia Sadar upazila, was arrested from Khoksa upazila, Kushtia, on the morning of Sunday 20 July 2025 by Islami University Thana police; there are at least six cases against him on human trafficking allegations, and he was to be taken to court on Monday 21 July with a remand application.
facts.source_in_article: OC Mehedi Hasan, Islami University Thana

facts.statement: Police sources say Robijul Islam was in Libya for about twelve years, acted there as the channel for taking young men from his area to Libya, and continued this after returning to Bangladesh; allegations of money dealings and human trafficking were raised against him at various times.

Police say Robijul lured village youths from Kushtia, Chuadanga, Jhenaidah and surrounding districts and sent them to Libya; after they arrived, ring members recorded videos of them suffering in Libya, sent the videos to the person's family and demanded large sums of money.
Police said Robijul was arrested after a preliminary investigation found the allegations true; he will be questioned about other members and police are working to identify the whole ring.
facts.source_in_article: OC Mehedi Hasan, Islami University Thana; police sources

headline_en: Five Bangladeshis in two Malaysian prisons; High Commission officials going to meet them
summary_en: Five Bangladeshis arrested in Malaysia and charged with terrorism-related offences are held in Selangor and Johor Bahru prisons, and Bangladesh High Commission officials were to visit them on Wednesday 9 July 2025 after prison authorities allowed consular access. Malaysia's home minister said 36 Bangladeshis were arrested over alleged links to Islamic State; High Commission sources put the number at 35, of whom 14 were visa overstayers handed to immigration and six of those have been sent back.

facts.statement: Five Bangladeshis arrested in Malaysia and charged with terrorism-related offences are being held in two prisons: two in Selangor prison and three in Johor Bahru prison.

Officials of the Bangladesh High Commission in Kuala Lumpur were to visit the five imprisoned Bangladeshis on Wednesday (9 July 2025) to give consular service, after Malaysia's prison authority gave permission; they will find out whether the men need legal or other basic assistance and hear any statement before deciding next steps.

On 27 June (2025) Malaysia's Home Minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail told the media that 36 Bangladeshis had been arrested in Malaysia on allegations of involvement with the militant group Islamic State (IS); he said police carried out the operation in three phases from 24 April in the Selangor and Johor areas.
facts.source_in_article: Malaysian Home Minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail

facts.statement: Of the 36 arrested Bangladeshis, five were charged with terrorism-related offences, expulsion (deportation) orders were issued against 15, and further investigation into militant links continues against the remaining 16.
facts.source_in_article: Prothom Alo report of the Malaysian minister's account

facts.statement: Bangladesh High Commission sources in Kuala Lumpur say that in separate operations by the Royal Malaysia Police counter-terrorism division from April to June 2025, 35 Bangladeshis were arrested, not 36. The article thus carries two figures (36 from the Malaysian minister, 35 from the High Commission).

Of the 35, 14 were staying in Malaysia illegally after their visas expired; those 14 were handed over to immigration police and six of them have been sent back to Bangladesh. Five were charged with terrorism offences and 16 remain under further investigation.

While the operation was under way, several Malaysian law-enforcement-linked bodies informally asked about a few Bangladeshis, including whether any had past militancy allegations; Bangladesh replied that none on the list had any such allegation in Bangladesh. The High Commission was not told then that a counter-terrorism operation was running.
facts.source_in_article: Bangladesh High Commission source; diplomatic source

facts.statement: Diplomatic sources in Dhaka and Kuala Lumpur say Bangladesh contacted Malaysia's foreign, home and human resources ministries from the start seeking assistance regarding the 35 detainees, but the High Commission did not get the expected response.
facts.source_in_article: Multiple diplomatic sources in Dhaka and Kuala Lumpur

key_quote_bn: তাঁদের মধ্যে ১৪ জন ভিসার মেয়াদ শেষ হওয়ার পরও অবৈধভাবে মালয়েশিয়ায় অবস্থান করছিলেন।

headline_en: Ringleader of gang that sent people to the Ukraine war in the name of jobs arrested
summary_en: CID says it arrested Muhammad Alamgir Hossain (40), the alleged ringleader of a gang that lured Bangladeshis with chocolate-factory cleaner or cook jobs in Russia at BDT 2 to 2.5 lakh a month, sent them first to Saudi Arabia on Umrah visas, then to Russia where they were handed to the Russian army and forced to fight Ukraine. At least one man was killed and one badly injured; another group of 10 is stranded in Saudi Arabia without passports. A partner of Dream Home Travels and Tours Limited, Banani, was arrested earlier.

facts.statement: CID claims it arrested the ringleader, Muhammad Alamgir Hossain (40), of Amtali Majherpara village, Lohagara thana, Chattogram, late at night last Wednesday (about 11 June 2025) at Shah Amanat Airport, Chattogram; he was shown arrested in a human trafficking case filed at Banani thana on 4 February (2025), gave a confessional statement at the Dhaka Chief Metropolitan Magistrate court and was sent to jail.

According to CID, the ring lured people with jobs as cleaners or cooks in a chocolate factory in Russia at a salary of BDT 2 to 2.5 lakh a month, first sent 10 people to Saudi Arabia on Umrah visas, had them perform Umrah, then took them to Russia and sold them to 'a Sultan', who handed them as slaves to Russian soldiers.

In Russia the victims were given military training and forced to fight against Ukraine; those who refused were physically and mentally tortured and their food was stopped to break their will, after which they joined the fighting under compulsion.
In the fighting, Humayun Kabir of Singra upazila, Natore, was killed and a man named Aminul of Keraniganj, Dhaka, was seriously wounded.

Md. Akram Hossain (24), of Palash thana, Narsingdi, one of the 10 sent to Russia, escaped from the training camp and returned to Bangladesh on 26 January (2025) by his own arrangement, then contacted the victims' families.

On information from returnee Akram Hossain, Jhumu Akter, wife of the war-wounded Aminul, filed a case at Banani thana, Dhaka, under the Prevention and Suppression of Human Trafficking Act (the case is dated 4 February 2025).

CID found that another group of 10 is in Saudi Arabia; after learning that people were being forced to fight, they refused to go to Russia, so their passports were taken away, and they can neither work in Saudi Arabia nor return home.

On the night of 5 February (2025) CID arrested Fabiha Jerin alias Tamanna, described as a key member of the trafficking ring, at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, Dhaka, while she was fleeing to Nepal; she is a partner of Dream Home Travels and Tours Limited in Banani, Dhaka.

CID Additional Special SP Md. Mostafizur Rahman said Alamgir went to Russia on a student visa in 2008, married there and got Russian citizenship; so far he has taken 50 people from Bangladesh to Russia on three categories of visa, and in the past year took 11 on work permit visas saying they would work in a Russian army camp, then forced them to fight Ukraine in breach of the terms.
facts.source_in_article: Md. Mostafizur Rahman, Additional Special Superintendent of Police, CID headquarters

facts.statement: Alamgir also took away the money the men received there, giving a list of costs he said had been spent under various heads.

CID has learned that three Bangladeshis have so far been killed fighting for Russia against Ukraine; the Russian government has confirmed two Bangladeshi deaths and said the process of sending their bodies to Bangladesh is under way.
CID says it is contacting the relevant government and non-government bodies to bring the victims home.

headline_en: Chief Adviser on his way home from Tokyo
summary_en: Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus left Tokyo on Saturday 31 May 2025 after a four-day official visit. Besides loan and grant announcements and six economic MoUs, two MoUs were signed on Thursday 29 May on raising Bangladeshi workers' skills and creating jobs for them in Japan, and Japanese authorities and businesses said they plan to recruit at least one lakh Bangladeshi workers over the next five years.

facts.statement: On Thursday 29 May 2025 two memoranda of understanding were signed between Bangladesh and Japan to increase Bangladeshi workers' skills and create employment opportunities for them in Japan, at a human resources seminar organised by the Bangladesh embassy at Hirakawacho, Chiyoda City, Tokyo, with Chief Adviser Yunus present.

At the Tokyo seminar Japanese authorities and business people said a plan has been made to recruit at least one lakh (100,000) Bangladeshi workers over the next five years to tackle Japan's growing labour shortage.
facts.source_in_article: Japanese authorities and business people at the seminar

facts.statement: On Friday 30 May 2025 Japan's Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba announced USD 106.3 crore (1.063 billion) of support for Bangladesh: USD 64.1 crore for railway development and reform, USD 41.8 crore for economic reform and climate resilience, and a USD 42 lakh grant for human development scholarships; the two leaders pledged to finalise a Bangladesh-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement within months.
Six memoranda of understanding on cooperation in economy, investment and other sectors were signed between Bangladesh and Japan at a 'Bangladesh Business Seminar' in Tokyo.

headline_en: 14 teenagers and young men rescued from traffickers' 'hostage house'
summary_en: BGB rescued 14 teenagers and young men at about 11:30 pm on Saturday 10 May 2025 from a locked room in a house at Uttar Lambori, Teknaf Sadar union, Cox's Bazar, where they were held for trafficking to Malaysia by sea while ransom was extracted from their families. Two victims from Cox's Bazar town said a CNG auto-rickshaw driver tricked them there from Inani; their families paid BDT 1 lakh each but they were still held 18 days. No one was detained.

facts.statement: At about 11:30 pm on Saturday 10 May 2025 a Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) team rescued 14 teenagers and young men from a house in the Uttar Lambori area of Teknaf Sadar union, Cox's Bazar; no one could be detained, and the rescued are in BGB custody.
facts.source_in_article: BGB; Lt Col Ashikur Rahman, commander, Teknaf-2 BGB Battalion

facts.statement: BGB says the 14 were kept locked in one room of the Teknaf house for the purpose of trafficking them to Malaysia by sea, and were held hostage there while money was extracted from their families.

Two rescued men, Mohammad Kasem and Mohin Uddin of Cox's Bazar town, said they had gone on an outing to the Inani area, where a CNG auto-rickshaw driver tricked them into going to the house in Teknaf; they were confined and beaten there.
facts.source_in_article: Victims Mohammad Kasem and Mohin Uddin

facts.statement: The families of Mohammad Kasem and Mohin Uddin were made to pay BDT 1 lakh each; even after the money was collected they were not freed but held in the house for 18 days, while attempts were made to sell them to brokers for trafficking to Malaysia by sea.
facts.source_in_article: Victims Mohammad Kasem and Mohin Uddin

facts.statement: BGB said it was trying to find out from the victims who was involved and would then take legal action against those responsible.
facts.source_in_article: Lt Col Ashikur Rahman, Teknaf-2 BGB Battalion

headline_en: Why air ticket prices are higher in Bangladesh
summary_en: A report comparing air fares from Dhaka with fares from Kolkata, New Delhi and Colombo for the same dates, finding Dhaka consistently dearer (for example Dhaka to Jeddah USD 552 against New Delhi to Jeddah USD 307 for 1 May 2025). Ticket sellers blame airlines' excess profit and a ticket-blocking ring; airlines blame high taxes, airport fees, fuel prices and delays in repatriating ticket revenue. The civil aviation ministry issued 10 directives in February 2025, including discounted tickets for migrant workers.

facts.statement: A direct Dhaka to Jeddah air ticket for 1 May (2025) was priced at USD 552 (about BDT 67,000), while a New Delhi to Jeddah ticket the same day was USD 307 (about BDT 37,500).
The lowest Dhaka to Bangkok fare found for 1 May (2025) was USD 231 (about BDT 28,000 at BDT 122 per dollar), against USD 167 from Kolkata and USD 140 from New Delhi the same day.

On Trip.com the lowest Dhaka-Singapore return fare (out 1 May, back 8 May 2025) was USD 409 (about BDT 50,000), against USD 277 (about BDT 34,000) for Kolkata-Singapore return on the same dates; Colombo to Singapore the same day was USD 206 (about BDT 25,000).
facts.source_in_article: Prothom Alo's own fare search on Trip.com

facts.statement: On one airline, Dhaka to Singapore on 1 May (2025) cost USD 271 (about BDT 33,000) while Singapore to Dhaka the same day cost USD 212 (about BDT 26,000) on Trip.com; on the airline's own website the fares were BDT 36,723 and BDT 26,817 respectively.
Before the Malaysian labour market closed in June of 'last year' (2024), ticket prices to Malaysia exceeded BDT 1 lakh; towards the end of that year a trade in tickets to Saudi Arabia began.

Ticket agencies say a ring formed during the previous Awami League government: state carrier Biman Bangladesh itself began charging more, blocking low-priced tickets and releasing only the higher-priced ones so everyone bought dear, after which the ring sold the low-priced tickets at high prices too; the practice has not fully stopped.

In February (2025) the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism issued 10 directives to prevent abnormal ticket prices; they say air tickets must be sold according to the price list approved by the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB) and that discounted tickets must be given to expatriate workers.
facts.source_in_article: Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism directive

facts.statement: A Home Ministry investigation committee recently found evidence of fraud behind high ticket prices and has submitted its report to the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism; a task force formed by the interim government is working on lowering ticket prices.

CAAB chairman Air Vice Marshal Md. Monjur Kabir Bhuiyan said CAAB does regular monitoring as regulator and has already written to all airlines to set the high and low ticket prices at a reasonable level.
facts.source_in_article: Air Vice Marshal Md. Monjur Kabir Bhuiyan, chairman, CAAB

facts.statement: Biman Bangladesh managing director Md. Safiqur Rahman said there is no longer any scope to block Biman tickets, anyone can book, Biman's ticket prices have fallen compared with before, and discounted tickets are being given to workers going abroad.
facts.source_in_article: Md. Safiqur Rahman, managing director, Biman Bangladesh

facts.statement: Aviation businesspeople say taking off from Dhaka costs at least 3 to 4 times more than from other countries; going from Dhaka to Singapore the tax per passenger is more than BDT 10,000, while on the return from Singapore the tax paid there is about BDT 3,000.

Aviation expert Kazi Wahidul Alam says that on an international ticket of BDT 1 lakh from Bangladesh, BDT 40,000 is government tax, with other fees on top; on a BDT 3,000 domestic ticket the government tax is BDT 1,100. He says Bangladesh's airport service quality is the lowest and its fees the highest.
facts.source_in_article: Kazi Wahidul Alam, aviation sector expert

facts.statement: Members of the Board of Airline Representatives (BAR) Bangladesh say foreign airlines' ticket revenue is remitted weekly in India, Nepal and Sri Lanka (two to three weeks at worst) but takes six to seven months from Bangladesh, sometimes over a year in a dollar shortage, with no interest; airlines now buy dollars at BDT 120 to 125 when remitting. The interim government has already reduced the remittance time.
facts.source_in_article: Members of Board of Airline Representatives (BAR) Bangladesh

facts.statement: Airlines say 75 percent of Bangladesh's air transport business is held by foreign companies, whereas in every country at least 50 percent is normally held by domestic carriers; ground handling at the airport is done solely by Biman Bangladesh.

The article says lakhs of Bangladeshi workers go abroad for work each year and more than one crore (10 million) expatriates live abroad; they are the airlines' main passengers and a large part of their income goes on air tickets.

ATAB president Abdus Salam Aref said Biman Bangladesh Airlines' ticket prices fell somewhat after the government circular of February (2025), that prices here are still higher than in other countries, and that CAAB could fix maximum and minimum fare limits.
facts.source_in_article: Abdus Salam Aref, president, Association of Travel Agents of Bangladesh (ATAB)

headline_en: Land of the yellow fairy-4
summary_en: A travelogue by a Bangladeshi postdoctoral researcher living in Taiwan about a five-day family trip to Singapore for a virology congress in November 2024. Most of it is sightseeing; the usable parts are his observations that Bangladeshis live around Little India where there are many cheap Bangladeshi restaurants, that most Bangladeshis he saw were working as cleaning and construction labourers, and small practical notes (EZ transport card, halal food, a paid-photo trick at the Singapore Flyer).

facts.statement: The writer observed that Bangladeshis in Singapore live around the Little India area, where there are many Bangladeshi restaurants; food there is quite cheap, with one plate carrying enough rice for three people.
facts.source_in_article: Writer Badruzzaman Khokon, postdoctoral researcher in Taiwan

facts.statement: The writer says he saw many Indians and Bangladeshis on Singapore's streets: Indians working in shops, malls and tourist sites, but most Bangladeshis working on the streets as cleaning, construction and other labourers.

The writer bought a mobile SIM and three EZ cards from a shop beside his hotel; the EZ card is used on public transport (he used mainly public buses and metro rail), and he says halal food shops are plentiful in Singapore.

At the Singapore Flyer a person offered to take the family's photo, saying it could be downloaded by scanning a barcode; the writer calls it a scam because on the way back they had to pay 70 Singapore dollars to buy the photos.

The writer, a Bangladeshi resident in Taiwan, applied for Singapore visas for three people at the Singapore business and cultural centre in Taipei (which handles visa work) at midday on 28 October and received visa confirmation by email on the morning of 30 October.
The writer states that about 16% of Singapore's population follow Islam.

key_quote_bn: বেশিরভাগ বাংলাদেশিকে দেখেছি রাস্তায়—ক্লিনিং, কনস্ট্রাকশনসহ নানা শ্রমিক হিসেবে কাজ করতে।

headline_en: 'Tell the government to bring my Mona back to my arms'
summary_en: Abdur Rab (25) of Kabirhat, Noakhali, who went to Libya in January 2022 on borrowed money and worked at a medicine manufacturer, was abducted on 14 January 2025 on the way to Misrata by people posing as law enforcement. Since 26 January his family has received torture videos and audio on imo with a ransom demand of BDT 26 lakh payable into five Bangladeshi bank accounts. His father has applied to the Deputy Commissioner, the Superintendent of Police and the district manpower office.

facts.statement: Abdur Rahim of Sundalpur village, Kabirhat upazila, Noakhali, says he borrowed from people and spent BDT 10 lakh to send his elder son Abdur Rab to Libya on 9 January 2022; the next year he sent his younger son Abdur Rahman the same way. Both brothers worked at a medicine manufacturing company in Libya, and much of the debt is still unpaid.

On 14 January (2025), on the way from their workplace to the city of Misrata, Abdur Rab, his brother Abdur Rahman and two others (four in all) were detained by people identifying themselves as law enforcement; after checking papers three were released but Abdur Rab was kept, and his brother could get no trace of him from the law-enforcement agencies afterwards.

On 26 January (2025) the family got a call on the imo app; the caller said they had bought Abdur Rab for BDT 20 lakh and would release him for BDT 26 lakh. When the father said he had no money, torture began.

Although the abduction was in Libya, the kidnappers told the family to pay the ransom into five bank accounts in Bangladesh and sent the account numbers along with audio recordings of torture; the father later learned the accounts were opened in Chattogram and Khulna.

A neighbour says the kidnappers recently sent two torture videos: one shows Abdur Rab with hands and feet tied with cloth being beaten on the soles of his feet, the other shows him being jabbed in the hand with a blade; they threatened to torture him to death if ransom was not paid.

The father applied to the Deputy Commissioner, the Superintendent of Police and the district office of the manpower and employment bureau for his son's rescue. The district office's assistant director Mukit Hasan said a complaint had been lodged with his office and he would arrange to send it through the ministry to the embassy in Libya.
facts.source_in_article: Abdur Rahim; Mukit Hasan, assistant director, district manpower and employment office, Noakhali

facts.statement: Noakhali Superintendent of Police Abdullah-Al-Faruk said the family's complaint had not come to his notice, that such matters involving expatriates are usually handled by the police Criminal Investigation Department (CID), and that he would still help on seeing a written complaint.

headline_en: 163 human trafficking cases filed so far in Mymensingh division, only two disposed of
summary_en: A divisional workshop in Mymensingh on 28 January 2025 on the national referral mechanism for trafficking victims heard that 163 human trafficking cases have been filed in the division and only two disposed of, because there is no tribunal. A Home Ministry joint secretary said trafficking victims would be able to file complaints online from 12 February 2025, with police, BGB and other units automatically notified.

facts.statement: 163 human trafficking cases have been filed in Mymensingh division so far and only two have been disposed of; the lack of a tribunal is given as the reason they cannot be disposed of quickly. Up to 2024 the cases were: Mymensingh district 52, Jamalpur 12, Netrokona 89, Sherpur 10.
facts.source_in_article: Statistics presented at the Mymensingh divisional workshop, 28 January 2025

facts.statement: A Home Ministry joint secretary said that from 12 February (2025) victims of human trafficking will be able to submit complaints online; once the complaint form is filled in, police, BGB and other relevant units will automatically receive the information and assist the victim, so victims will not face harassment.
facts.source_in_article: Mu. Jasim Uddin Khan, joint secretary, Public Security Division, Ministry of Home Affairs

facts.statement: INCIDIN Bangladesh's executive director said the real number of trafficking cases is far higher than published statistics, as many victims do not dare to file cases because of social and legal complications, though Mymensingh division has comparatively fewer than other divisions.
facts.source_in_article: A K M Masud Ali, executive director, INCIDIN Bangladesh

facts.statement: The Mymensingh Deputy Commissioner said human trafficking is taking place through the two border upazilas of Mymensingh district, Haluaghat and Dhobaura, and that BGB needs to be more active.

The workshop, titled on the Bangladesh National Referral Mechanism framework for protection and assistance of trafficking victims, was organised by the Public Security Division of the Home Ministry and the Mymensingh divisional administration at the district council auditorium on Tuesday 28 January 2025.

key_quote_bn: আগামী ১২ ফেব্রুয়ারি থেকে মানবপাচারের ভিকটিমরা অনলাইনে অভিযোগ জমা দিতে পারবেন।

headline_en: National Expatriates' Day observed in Amman
summary_en: The Bangladesh embassy in Amman, Jordan, marked National Expatriates' Day and International Migrants Day on Wednesday 18 December 2024 with a discussion and cultural programme. The ambassador urged workers in Jordan to send remittances through legal channels and promised work on expatriate voting rights and remittance-related legal complications; the first secretary (labour) said many Bangladeshis work in Jordan's garment sector and as domestic workers, and asked them not to work illegally.

facts.statement: Bangladesh's ambassador to Jordan, Nure Helal Saifur Rahman, called on all Bangladeshi migrants working in Jordan to send remittances home through legal channels.

The ambassador said expatriate Bangladeshis face various legal complications in sending money home and the embassy is working to reduce them; he also said Bangladeshis working abroad are deprived of the right to vote in national elections and the embassy would work on steps to ensure it.

The embassy's first secretary (labour) said a large number of Bangladeshi workers are employed in Jordan's garment sector, and many Bangladeshis are also in domestic work, housing and other businesses.
facts.source_in_article: Umme Salma, first secretary (labour), Bangladesh embassy in Amman

facts.statement: The first secretary (labour) told Bangladeshi migrant workers in Jordan that the embassy is with them for any need and asked them not to work illegally in Jordan.
facts.source_in_article: Umme Salma, first secretary (labour), Bangladesh embassy in Amman

headline_en: Dollar price in the country crosses BDT 127
summary_en: In December 2024 banks in Bangladesh began buying remittance dollars at up to BDT 127.50, up from BDT 121-122 before December, because Bangladesh Bank ordered old import liabilities settled within the month; the open-market rate also passed BDT 127. The article lists the rates paid by named remittance houses and gives remittance inflow figures for December 2024, November 2024 and December 2023.

facts.statement: Before December (2024) banks bought remittance dollars from expatriates at BDT 121-122 per dollar; in December this rose to BDT 127.50. Banks were still selling cash dollars at BDT 123, and the card rate (credit and other cards) was BDT 123.

Remittance house sources say Sonali Exchange Company bought dollars at BDT 124, Ria Money Exchange at BDT 124.18, Taptap Send at BDT 124.70 and Western Union at BDT 125.60, so banks had to buy from them at higher prices.

In Dhaka's open (kerb) market the dollar was being bought at BDT 126.70 and sold at BDT 127.50; ten days earlier it was bought at BDT 122.50 and sold at BDT 123. The price rose at least BDT 4 in a little over a week.

In the first 14 days of December 2024 remittances of USD 138.13 crore came in, a daily average of about USD 9.8669 crore; in the whole of December 2023 remittances were USD 199.1260 crore (daily average USD 6.4234 crore); in November 2024 they were USD 220 crore.
facts.source_in_article: Prothom Alo report (Bangladesh Bank data implied)

facts.statement: Bank officials say Bangladesh Bank ordered banks to pay off old import liabilities within the month, so from early December several state-owned banks and one private bank began buying remittance dollars at higher prices and others had to follow; higher rates are bringing in more remittances.

Mutual Trust Bank MD Syed Mahbubur Rahman said dollars are not available from all remittance houses as before: some companies buy up dollars from smaller companies and banks must buy from them at higher prices. He said the rise is temporary and expected the price to fall in January.
facts.source_in_article: Syed Mahbubur Rahman, managing director, Mutual Trust Bank

facts.statement: Bangladesh Bank's foreign exchange reserves rose by USD 19 crore in a week to USD 2,494 crore on Wednesday (18 December 2024), from USD 2,475 crore the previous Wednesday, as the central bank bought dollars from commercial banks.
Sector people say one reason for the open-market rise is sharply higher demand for dollars from outbound travellers, as many go abroad for holidays in December.

key_quote_bn: ডিসেম্বরের আগে তারা প্রবাসীদের কাছ থেকে প্রতি ডলার কিনত ১২১-১২২ টাকায়। এখন তা বেড়ে ১২৭ টাকা ৫০ পয়সায় উঠেছে।

headline_en: EU-funded Talent Partnership project launched
summary_en: A EUR 3 million EU-funded Talent Partnership project was formally launched in Dhaka on Wednesday 11 December 2024. ILO, the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment and BMET will implement it over 2024-27 to train 3,000 workers to the skill standards EU labour markets need, upgrade the ministry's online job platform, cut migration costs and reduce irregular migration.

facts.statement: A EUR 30 lakh (3 million) Talent Partnership project funded by the European Union was formally launched in Dhaka on Wednesday 11 December 2024; it aims to address workers' skill gaps, reduce migration costs and widen opportunities for Bangladeshis wishing to migrate for work so as to supply skilled workers for the EU labour market.

The International Labour Organization (ILO), the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment (MoEWOE) and the Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET) will implement the project over three years, 2024-27.

The project's training programmes aim to prepare 3,000 workers with the skills required for employment in the EU, training them to the skill standards needed in various sectors of EU member states' labour markets, with emphasis on safe, dignified legal migration routes and reducing irregular migration.
The project will also make the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment's online platform fit for job matching (finding jobs).
The article states that more than 74 lakh (7.4 million) Bangladeshi migrant workers send EUR 200 crore (2 billion) in remittances every month.

EU ambassador Michael Miller said the EU-Bangladesh Talent Partnership will ensure safe and dignified migration and that, alongside creating legal migration pathways, work must be stepped up to end irregular migration and tackle trafficking and exploitation; ILO country director Tuomo Poutiainen said it aims to facilitate technical skills development and fair recruitment; adviser Asif Nazrul said it will ensure workers' safety and raise remittances.
facts.source_in_article: Michael Miller, EU ambassador; Tuomo Poutiainen, ILO country director; adviser Asif Nazrul

key_quote_bn: প্রশিক্ষণ প্রোগ্রামগুলো ইইউতে কর্মসংস্থানের জন্য প্রয়োজনীয় দক্ষতা পূরণের জন্য তিন হাজার কর্মীকে প্রস্তুত করার লক্ষ্যে কাজ করবে।

headline_en: The word 'non-resident' remains in the notification; fear that investment will be hampered
summary_en: The government has reopened the Wage Earners' Development Bond to seafarers, pilots and cabin crew after more than four years and removed the investment ceiling, by an Internal Resources Division notification effective 1 December 2024. The merchant marine officers' association fears the word 'non-resident' left in the notification will cause trouble, since seafarers on 4 to 9 month contracts cannot prove residence in any one country; the IRD secretary says a clarification will be issued if needed. The article restates the bond's terms.

facts.statement: By a notification of the Internal Resources Division (IRD), which this article dates 4 November (2024), the government reopened investment in the Wage Earners' Development Bond for seafarers, pilots and cabin crew after more than four years and removed the upper limit on investment in the bond; the notification takes effect from 1 December (2024).
facts.source_in_article: IRD notification, as reported by Prothom Alo

facts.statement: The notification retains the word 'non-resident'; the Bangladesh Merchant Marine Officers' Association (BMMOA) fears it may be read as requiring the investor to reside in the country concerned, causing complications for seafarers. Its vice-president says they had asked IRD officials before the notification to drop the word and believe it was left in by mistake.

BMMOA argues that seafarers have no pension, provident fund or post-retirement benefit; a Bangladeshi marine officer on a foreign-flag ship is under that country's jurisdiction under international law; contracts usually run 4 to 9 months; and he cannot show proof of residence in any particular country for the whole period, though sign-on to sign-off records are internationally valid documents.

IRD secretary Md. Abdur Rahman Khan said the notification names the professions, so there should be no trouble investing in the bond; if there is, IRD will look into it and issue an amendment or clarification if necessary.
facts.source_in_article: Md. Abdur Rahman Khan, secretary, IRD

facts.statement: The Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment had recently written to the IRD secretary saying the ceiling on the Wage Earners' Development Bond should be lifted to raise expatriates' investment alongside remittance flow.

The Wage Earners' Development Bond is a five-year bond introduced in Bangladesh in 1981 paying profit on a simple-interest basis; under the Wage Earners' Development Bond Rules 1981 (amended 23 May 2015) any amount could be invested in it.

Wage Earners' Development Bonds can be bought at Bangladesh Bank, exchange houses, exchange companies, and the foreign and authorised dealer (AD) branches of scheduled banks; a foreign currency (FC) account is not required to buy them.
Profit on the Wage Earners' Development Bond is income-tax-free, loans can be taken against the bond, and investment carries a death-risk benefit of 40 to 50 percent.

The foreign-currency earner (wage earner) can invest in the Wage Earners' Development Bond personally or in the name of a person he or she nominates; government employees working at Bangladesh embassies abroad can also invest.

On 3 December 2020 the Internal Resources Division (IRD) set a combined investment ceiling equivalent to BDT 1 crore in foreign currency for the Wage Earners' Development Bond, US Dollar Premium Bond and US Dollar Investment Bond, and at the same time barred seafarers, pilots and cabin crew from the wage earners' bond. On 4 April 2022 the ceiling on the two US dollar bonds was lifted, but the ceiling on the Wage Earners' Development Bond stayed and its automatic reinvestment was also stopped.

key_quote_bn: এই বন্ডের মুনাফা আয়করমুক্ত। বন্ডের বিপরীতে ঋণ নেওয়ার সুযোগও আছে।

headline_en: Some new benefits for investing in savings certificates and bonds
summary_en: The interim government has announced new facilities for investors in national savings certificates and bonds, including expatriate Bangladeshis, by an IRD notification effective 1 December 2024. The ceiling on the Wage Earners' Development Bond is withdrawn, it can be reinvested for two further terms, the US Dollar Premium and Investment Bonds for four, and seafarers, pilots and cabin crew of foreign-owned companies can again invest. The article also covers automatic reinvestment for domestic savings certificates and restates the bond's terms.

facts.statement: The investment ceiling on the Wage Earners' Development Bond has been withdrawn; money can be invested for 1 term and reinvested for 2 terms. The IRD notification was issued on Sunday 3 November 2024 ('yesterday Sunday' in an article published 4 November) and takes effect from 1 December 2024.
facts.source_in_article: IRD notification; IRD secretary Abdur Rahman Khan

facts.statement: For the US Dollar Premium Bond and US Dollar Investment Bond, investment for 1 term and reinvestment for 4 terms has been allowed.

Non-resident Bangladeshi seafarers (mariners), pilots and cabin crew employed in the overseas offices of foreign-owned shipping or airways companies, whom the previous government had barred, can again invest in the Wage Earners' Development Bond, with no upper limit on the amount.
For national savings schemes with automatic reinvestment, the investment ceiling will apply from the date of reinvestment.

New facilities for domestic savings certificates: automatic reinvestment of principal for the Three-Monthly Profit Sanchayapatra and Paribar Sanchayapatra; for Pensioner Sanchayapatra automatic reinvestment of principal plus profit paid monthly instead of quarterly; for the five-year Bangladesh Sanchayapatra and Post Office Savings Bank fixed deposit, reinvestment of principal together with profit.

The government's target is to raise BDT 15,400 crore from savings certificate sales in fiscal 2024-25; the National Savings Directorate says net sales are trending negative again, meaning encashment exceeds sales.

BMMOA says the number of Bangladeshi seafarers (the profession barred from the bond in 2020) is now more than 12,000; they have no pension, provident fund or post-retirement benefit and usually work on 4 to 9 month contracts.

The Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment wrote to the IRD secretary two months before (the November 2024 article) saying the ceiling on the Wage Earners' Development Bond should be lifted to raise expatriates' investment alongside remittance flow.

The Wage Earners' Development Bond is a five-year bond introduced in Bangladesh in 1981 paying profit on a simple-interest basis; under the Wage Earners' Development Bond Rules 1981 (amended 23 May 2015) any amount could be invested in it.

Wage Earners' Development Bonds can be bought at Bangladesh Bank, exchange houses, exchange companies, and the foreign and authorised dealer (AD) branches of scheduled banks; a foreign currency (FC) account is not required to buy them.
Profit on the Wage Earners' Development Bond is income-tax-free, loans can be taken against the bond, and investment carries a death-risk benefit of 40 to 50 percent.

The foreign-currency earner (wage earner) can invest in the Wage Earners' Development Bond personally or in the name of a person he or she nominates; government employees working at Bangladesh embassies abroad can also invest.

On 3 December 2020 the Internal Resources Division (IRD) set a combined investment ceiling equivalent to BDT 1 crore in foreign currency for the Wage Earners' Development Bond, US Dollar Premium Bond and US Dollar Investment Bond, and at the same time barred seafarers, pilots and cabin crew from the wage earners' bond. On 4 April 2022 the ceiling on the two US dollar bonds was lifted, but the ceiling on the Wage Earners' Development Bond stayed and its automatic reinvestment was also stopped.

key_quote_bn: ওয়েজ আর্নার্স ডেভেলপমেন্ট বন্ডে বিনিয়োগের ঊর্ধ্বসীমা প্রত্যাহার করা হয়েছে।

headline_en: Growth in remittances is the main reason reserves rose
summary_en: A reader's opinion piece by a Bangladeshi in Kuwait saying the rise in remittances in July-August 2024 stopped the fall in Bangladesh's reserves, yet expatriates get no recognition. He alleges embassies do not help workers in trouble and that there are complaints of harassment, asks for respectful treatment at the airport, interest-free loans for people going abroad and simpler processing.

facts.statement: The writer says remittance flow rose considerably in July to August (2024), that this is the main reason foreign exchange reserves increased, and that Bangladesh Bank believes the fall in reserves has been halted.
facts.source_in_article: Writer Saif Al Rubel, Bangladeshi expatriate in Kuwait

facts.statement: The writer alleges that when expatriates fall into trouble abroad the Bangladesh embassy gives no help, and that there are also complaints of harassment in various ways; he asks that expatriates not be harassed at the airport and be treated politely.

The writer demands interest-free loans for people going abroad, simpler processing for going abroad, easier arrangement of work for Bangladeshis in different countries, and easier financial assistance for those who need it.

key_quote_bn: বিদেশগামীদের জন্য বিনা সুদে ঋণের ব্যবস্থা করা হোক
